title: Operator dashboard wireframe for prefetch warmth and soft fallbacks
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a compact, operator-focused dashboard wireframe for monitoring KV-prefetch/kvcache warmth, prefetch health, and soft-fallback behavior across tenant cohorts. Intended for SREs and runtime owners to triage cold-cache incidents, detect degrading prefetch effectiveness, and watch fallback routing spikes that affect UI perceived latency.

Context and motivation:
- We observed frequent transient latency spikes during high-burst traffic where prefix warmup is inconsistent. Operator feedback: current dashboards surface cache eviction and overall hit-rate, but not prefetching success nor how often requests hit fallback model variants.
- Goal: provide a single-pane (microdash) for fast triage: 1) kv-warmth and prefetch success, 2) fallback count and reason, 3) impact on TTF token quantiles, 4) tenant hot/cold breakdown.

Audience and constraints:
- Primary: night-ops / oncall engineers and SRE rotation (30m timebox to triage). Secondary: platform PMs for rollout gating. Must be cheap to query (<1s widget queries) and use low-cardinality aggregates by default with links to high-cardinality drilldowns.

Suggested signal set (metric definitions) — canonical names and short definitions (for implementation):
1) inference.kv_prefetch.attempts.count: total prefetch attempts (per model, per region).
2) inference.kv_prefetch.success.count: successful prefetch writes to KV (key materialization completed).
3) inference.kv_cache.hit_rate.p50/p95: percent hits over window (tenant-scoped optional).
4) inference.kv_cache.warmth.index: fraction of recent active prefixes with warm KV entries (rolling 1h).
5) inference.kv_cache.evictions.rate: evictions per minute (by host/gpu-pool).
6) inference.fallbacks.count: number of requests routed to fallback variants (labels: reason=[capacity, timeout, error, policy]).
7) ttf.first-token.ms.p50/p95 (by model_variant and fallback=true/false).
8) request.pathology.rate: percent of requests with >1 fallback hop or error-class leading to user-visible degrade.
9) tenant.prefetch.success_ratio: per-tenant ratio (small_tenants aggregated into "small" bin by default).

Tracing/span tags and expectations:
- Span name: service:inference->model:prefetch_write (duration, status).
- Important tags: tenant_id, model_variant, prefetch_trigger=[prefix, explicit_probe, synthetic], eviction_reason, fallback_reason, node_pool.
- Trace sampling guidance: sample 1/1000 requests globally, increase to 1/100 of requests when fallback rate > 0.5% over 5m for targeted tenants. Attach full kv-prefetch span sequence on sampled traces.

Dashboard wireframe (operator microdash):
Top row: quick health + signal anchors (1 row, 4 tiles)
- Tile A: KV Warmth Index (sparkline last 12h) — query: avg(inference.kv_cache.warmth.index{region}) by region. Threshold color: <0.65 amber, <0.4 red.
- Tile B: Prefetch success ratio (global, 5m) — show absolute attempts and success percent.
- Tile C: Fallback rate (global 5m) — stacked by reason label.
- Tile D: TTF delta for fallback vs baseline (p95 difference) — callout if >150ms.

Second row: heatmap / cohort breakdown (1 row)
- Widget: Tenant warmth heatmap: x-axis top N tenants by request rate, y-axis warmth over 24h (color = warmth index). Clicking tenant drills to tenant detail.

Third row: incident probes and traces (2 columns)
- Left: Prefetch attempt latency distribution by region/model (histogram). Highlight tails > 200ms.
- Right: Recent traces list — show traces where fallback=true or eviction_reason present. Columns: time, tenant, model_variant, fallback_reason, trace_link.

Bottom row: operators tools and quick queries (single row)
- Quick action buttons (links): re-run prefetch for tenant (internal API link), bump prefetch parallelism for a pool (RBAC guarded), create incident prefilled.
- Embedded query box: sample SQL/PromQL snippets for fast triage.

Example PromQL/snippets (operator-ready):
- Prefetch success ratio (5m): sum(inference_kv_prefetch_success_count[5m]) / sum(inference_kv_prefetch_attempts_count[5m])
- Global fallback rate (5m): sum(inference_fallbacks_count[5m]) / sum(inference_requests_total[5m])
- Warmth index (rolling 1h): avg_over_time(inference_kv_cache_warmth_index[1h])
- Top tenants with fallback spikes (5m): topk(20, sum by (tenant_id) (increase(inference_fallbacks_count[5m])))

Alerting heuristics (suggestions):
- P0: fallback rate > 5% sustained for >5m and resulting p95 TTF increase >200ms (pager).
- P1: kv_warmth_index < 0.35 for >15m for >=3 high-volume tenants (pager to SRE rotation + slack).
- P2: prefetch success_ratio < 70% global for 10m (Slack, ops-ticket).
- Noise controls: only alert on tenant-level when tenant request volume > X req/min (configurable), otherwise create aggregated incident.

Drilldown playbooks (short):
1) If fallback rate rises: check fallbacks.count labels -> if reason=capacity, check pool utilization widgets and autoscaling logs. If reason=timeout or error, open recent traces (widget) and inspect prefetch spans.
2) If warmth index drops: inspect evictions.rate by host -> investigate release/eviction changes (recent deployments). Run targeted synthetic probe for a sample tenant to validate prefetch path.
3) If p95 TTF delta spikes: compare p95 for fallback=true vs baseline. If baseline unchanged, high fallback p95 indicates fallback model throttling.

Operational notes and tradeoffs (notes to self):
- Keep cardinality low on the microdash; default groupings should be region/model band/tenant-size-bucket. Full tenant-level panels live in a drilldown dashboard.
- Cost: prefer counters/gauge rollups over raw trace exports. Use adaptive trace sampling to capture edge cases without exorbitant S3/trace costs.
- UX: color semantics must unify with other infra dashboards (green: healthy, amber: actionable, red: urgent).

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to encode "prefetch trigger" from client — do we rely on request header or runtime inference logic? Action: ENG-2147 follow-up (Carlos) to standardize header.
- Decide the tenant volume threshold for tenant-level alerts (proposal: 10 req/s).
- Add a synthetic probe family that validates full prefetch->use path with deterministic keys; track synthetic.prefetch.success. (PR: github PR/392 notes).
- Instrument eviction reason more finely (OOM vs TTL vs manual).

Implementation tasks (short backlog):
- (Priya) add inference.kv_prefetch.* counters and eviction_reason label: 2w.
- (Noah) dashboard wireframe prototype in Grafana: 1w.
- (Carlos) sampling policy for traces and trace-attach logic: 1w.
- (Maya) alerting rules + runbook draft and Slack routing: 3d.

Appendix: quick glossary for oncall
- Warmth index: fraction of prefixes that have valid, warm KV entries and are likely to be hit without remote load.
- Prefetch success: prefetch flow completed and write persisted to KV store (not necessarily used).
- Fallback: request routed to non-primary model_variant due to policy/capacity/error.

Notes to reviewers: this is an operator-first sketch. Expect to iterate. Please add comments inline (Confluence link above) with concrete metric names and label schema suggestions.
